clue.text: Coming from this country, 1 celebrate being brought under state control

parts.note: something national belongs to or comes from one's own country

explanation.surface: A patriot sings the praises of a state takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 as printed is read as I (one); the clue may simply have been set as 'I celebrate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationalising an industry puts it into public ownership, run by the government.

clue.text: A woman last month embracing males, and this is the end of the marriage

parts.note: ult., short for ultimo, means last month in old business letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'ult.' (ultimo) is old commercial shorthand for last month.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulment declares a marriage void, bringing it formally to a close.

clue.text: Fire made from using less coal

explanation.definitionFit: A neatherd is an old word for a cowherd, a keeper of cattle.

explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' is a link: the fool comes after the time word, which comes after the abbreviation for second.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow goose is a white Arctic-breeding wild goose.

clue.text: Animal which appears in any alarming situation

explanation.surface: Absorb the intricate detail, as if it were a bird's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A swallow's tail is deeply forked, and a swallow-tailed coat has two such tails at the back.

clue.text: Please now halt distribution of deadly armaments

explanation.definitionFit: Port wine is served in a small stemmed glass, so that glass is where the drink is found.

clue.text: Speak language about an animal

a thing that works functions properly

clue.text: Tired feeling when one is between river and headland

clue.text: I act up in crops rearranged for versification
